title: Main draft implementation: broadcast-scope mention types
description:
Implement the design decisions from jmap-chat-spec-fig9.1 in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md.

Blocked on jmap-chat-spec-fig9.1.

This bead is BLOCKING for jmap-chat-spec-fig9.3 (push), .4 (federation), .5 (push platform guide) — those depend on the main draft having committed wire-format definitions.

Likely scope (assumes Path A for Decision 1, extend-existing for Decision 2, umbrella for Decision 3):
- Extend Mention type at line 263 with `type` field and conditional `id`
- Extend rich-body `"mention"` span at line 1285 with `scope` field
- Update mention validation at line 1461 to handle new types (no `id` for broadcasts; `offset + length` still bounds-checked)
- Update Message/set send-side authorization to gate broadcast mentions on `mention_all` permission
- Update server behavior on inbound delivery to compute recipient set per Decision 4
- Add suppression-preference handling per Decision 5 (may add new fields to Chat or PresenceStatus)
- Update the Mention type IANA-style example at line 1296 (rich-body example) to show a broadcast mention

Does NOT include: push payload changes (separate bead), federation Peer/deliver changes (separate bead), implementer-guide updates (separate bead).
acceptance_criteria:
- Mention type extended; Mention validation updated
- Rich-body span model extended; existing example updated
- Send-side authorization rules updated (with "Requires X" wording consistent with §Authorization clarification)
- Receiver-side recipient-set computation rules added per Decision 4
- Suppression handling per Decision 5
- All cross-references resolve; no broken anchors
- Spec corpus consistency check: grep for old field shapes returns expected matches; new fields appear where expected
close_reason: Implemented per fig9.1 decision record (Path B, D2-A, umbrella-renamed permission, hybrid resolution, D5-Impl, M1 all-at-once). Main draft only; push draft (fig9.4), federation (fig9.3), and implementer guide (newly filed fig9.6) are tracked separately.
